patent.title: Method and system for manipulating the architecture and the content of a document separately from each other
patent.family_note: The appellate opinion identifies i4i as the patent owner at the 2010 litigation T0. Current post-T0 legal-status information is not used to upgrade the historical state.

knowledge_origin.description: This first non-award pressure test does not reconstruct the complete R&D genealogy behind the 1994 invention.

technology.problem: Edit documents containing markup while separating document structure/metacodes from document content.
technology.mechanism: The asserted invention stores document content and metacodes separately, including use of a metacode map distinct from mapped content.

value_carriers.name: Microsoft Word custom XML editor
value_carriers.description: The appellate judgment records infringement of asserted claims by the custom XML editor in certain Microsoft Word versions.

value_links.note: Implementation is established through adjudicated infringement, not through a voluntary license or owner-provided product map.
The injunction is evidence of enforceability/control in this specific dispute and time period.

value_metrics.note: Directly tied to litigation over U.S. Patent 5,787,449, but not an intrinsic patent price. The appellate court did not reach the sufficiency/reasonableness of the amount because the challenge was not preserved.

gaps.description: The litigation record establishes infringement and enforcement outcomes but this ledger does not yet construct a field-normalized technological-quality comparison.

V0.7 can record R5/E4 and the injunction as evidence, but cannot explicitly model rights-control dimensions such as claim scope, validity resilience, remaining term, design-around conditions and counterfactual blocking power.

notes: First non-award V0.8 pressure-test archetype. The case is selected for mechanism coverage, not award status. The $200m figure is preserved as dispute-specific patent-level evidence and explicitly not treated as an intrinsic or universal patent price.
